Hi Jane / Mark — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps on the PII / prompt-output questions we discussed: 

- What we store by default (Hosted API): request metadata (request id, timestamps, token counts, latency) and full request/response payloads (prompts and model outputs) are retained for 30 days by default to support debugging, billing, and abuse detection.
- Model training: Redwood does NOT use customer prompts or outputs to retrain or improve public models unless a customer explicitly opts in via a separate data-sharing agreement.
- Embeddings: stored only if you choose to persist them (e.g., for retrieval use); otherwise embeddings can be disabled/ephemeral.
- Dedicated / Private deployments: you control retention and can disable storing full request/response logs entirely. We provide options to configure retention windows and storage locations.
- Data residency: Hosted accounts are provisioned in the region you select (US/EU); logs are stored in that region by default. Dedicated/Private gives you full control (VPC/KMS integration).
- Encryption & keys: data at rest is encrypted; for Dedicated/Private we offer customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM).

Attached: SOC2-Summary.pdf and a copy of our DPA (DPA-redline.docx).

Ask: Can you confirm whether Acme would prefer Hosted with the 30-day default retention or if you want to evaluate Dedicated/Private options (we can prepare a configuration matrix and cost estimate)? Also, Mark — you asked for a short paragraph we can use in procurement language; I’ll loop in Neha from Product/Security to provide that.

Thanks,

Hi Mark / Jane — thanks for the clear questions. Below is a short procurement-ready paragraph followed by detailed confirmations for your team to reference.

Procurement paragraph (2–3 sentences):
"Redwood Inference does not use customer prompts or model outputs to train or improve public models unless the customer explicitly opts in via a written data-sharing agreement. By default, Hosted accounts retain request/response payloads (prompts and outputs) and associated metadata for 30 days; retention and full logging can be configured or disabled in Dedicated and Private deployments. Data is stored in the region selected at account provisioning (US or EU), encrypted at rest, and can be secured with customer-managed KMS keys for Dedicated/Private deployments."

Detailed confirmations:
- What is stored by default (Hosted): full prompt text and raw model outputs are stored for 30 days by default. Associated metadata (request id, timestamps, token counts, client IPs and headers used for debugging) are also logged. Embeddings are only persisted if the customer opts to store them; otherwise embedding generation can be ephemeral.
- Retention: default retention is 30 days for Hosted; this window can be shortened for Hosted on request (subject to billing/debugging tradeoffs) and can be fully controlled for Dedicated/Private (including indefinite retention or immediate deletion).
- Model improvement: Redwood will NOT use customer prompts/outputs to improve public or internal models unless a customer explicitly opts in under a separate agreement. Aggregated telemetry (non-content metrics like latency, error rates, token counts) may be used for product improvements.
- Data residency: Hosted accounts are provisioned in the selected region (US or EU); logs and payloads are stored in that region. For EU residency requirements we recommend a Dedicated or Private deployment where you control the VPC and storage location.
- Encryption & KMS: data at rest is encrypted; for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed KMS/HSM keys.
- Evidence & compliance: SOC 2 Type II summary attached; we can provide a DPA and sign a narrow data processing addendum as needed.

Next steps: I can convert the procurement paragraph into a one-line clause for your DPA if you want, or we can schedule a short call with our Compliance lead to walk through the artifacts. Let me know which you prefer.

Thanks,
